title: Exploring Experimental Evidence for Diffusional Creep Mechanisms in Alloys
content: Seventy-five years ago, Nabarro and Herring (N-H) and subsequently Coble, theorized Newtonian diffusional creep mechanisms in crystalline materials [1, 2]. They postulated that the deformation rate was governed by the flow of atoms along the direction of applied stress via a vacancy-atom exchange mechanism. These theories provide a compelling framework for materials scientists to design microstructures with improved creep resistance. However, they remain vigorously debated due to a lack of direct experimental evidence and poor predictions of the observed creep rates in certain materials and conditions [3-5]. To validate the diffusional creep mechanisms, we hypothesized that in alloys undergoing diffusional creep, elemental redistribution would manifest at nearby grain boundaries if the diffusivities of the alloying elements were significantly different. Furthermore, we hypothesized that the extent of elemental redistribution would vary depending on the orientation of the grain boundary with respect to the tensile loading axis.
